newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs end weak on fund rolling, liquidation.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs end weak on fund rolling, liquidation.

text.p: Rolling by funds and long commercial liquidation added to technical pressure and knocked CME hog futures to lower closes, traders said. Pork bellies slipped at the close after rallying for net gains from sharp early losses, traders said.
Hog futures ended 0.900 to 0.100 cent per lb lower paced by December. Pork bellies closed 0.150 to 2.000 cent lower with February 0.275 lower at 73.825 cents.
Rolling of fund positions, know as the "Goldman roll", by Refco and Cargill Investor Services added to earlier technical pressure and commercial selling, traders said.

Goldman Sachs, normally over a five-day period, rolls its positions into the next month used in calculating its commodity indexes. The "roll" that began last Thursday should have been completed, traders said.
The fund action added to developing fundamental weakness. Commercial selling came on expectations that hog runs will soon increase and cash prices slip, sources said.
"Producers may be holding back some of their (hog) marketings out here (Iowa)" and that will lead to more marketings later, said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities Inc.
Recent higher hog weights may mean hogs are being held back, traders said.
For instance, USDA reported the average market hog weight in Iowa/Minnesota direct trade the week ended November 9 was 254.5 lbs, up from 253.7 lbs the prior week and above 253.6 lbs a year earlier.
Roose also cited developing weakness in cash ham prices which may indicate holiday buying of hams is over, he said.
USDA, in its midday carlot pork report, quoted 17 to 20 lb hams mostly $2.00 per cwt lower and 20 to 26 lb hams steady.
Technicals added to weakness as the market appeared to be consolidating and correcting from recent gains.
"It looks to me like its (December) consolidating under the contract high. Fundamentals are not breaking, but the market is overbought," said Julia Bussie with AG Edwards.
Rand Financials and Rosenthal Collins notably sold early before the late fund action, pit sources said.
In hog options, Cargill bought October 64 calls early. Traders offered December puts late after the break in futures. Volatility in February and April was firm, pit sources added.
Pork bellies recovered from early declines linked to Tuesday's bearish CME out-of-town report.

Futures posted net gains before slipping again at the close on renewed local selling following action in hog futures. Locals had covered short positions on the rally which stemmed from higher pork values. Rand was a notable buyer on the advance after selling early along with Refco and LIT division of First Options, traders said.

CME reported a net in-movement last week of 2.83 million lbs versus expectations of 1.5 million to 2.0 million lbs net in. But cash belly prices continued to rise and 14-16 lb bellies ranged up to $67 per cwt at noon, the highest level since October 10.
